How to Get More Salon Bookings From Google Maps

Nov 2, 2026The SocialDM Insights Team6 min read
Key takeaways
  • Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence, and you cannot pay for a better Maps ranking.
  • Service searches like "balayage near me" reward salons that name those services clearly on their profile and website.
  • Real, recent, permission-cleared photos of your work act as your portfolio on Maps.
  • Steady reviews with thoughtful replies, plus a booking link that works on a phone, turn views into appointments.
In this article
  1. What decides which salons show up for "hair salon near me"?
  2. Why do some salons show up for "balayage near me" and others do not?
  3. What does a strong salon Google Business Profile look like?
  4. Do photos really matter on Google Maps?
  5. How much do reviews matter for salon bookings?

When someone searches "hair salon near me" or "balayage near me," Google shows a short list of salons on the map, and most guests choose from that list. Google says those local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. You cannot move your chair closer to every guest, so the salons that win bookings from Maps are the ones with a complete, accurate profile that clearly matches the service, real photos of their work, a steady flow of reviews and a booking button that works on a phone.

Referrals and walk-ins still matter. But even a guest whose friend sent them will usually look you up first, and what they see on Maps decides whether they book or keep scrolling.

What decides which salons show up for "hair salon near me"?

Google's own page on how to improve local ranking names three main factors. Relevance is how well your Business Profile matches what the person searched. Distance is how far you are from them, or from the place they named. Prominence is how well known your salon is, and Google says reviews count toward it, with more reviews and positive ratings able to help.

The same page says complete and accurate business information helps Google match you to the right searches, and that there is no way to pay for a better local ranking. Ads are a separate product. So the work that moves the needle is not a trick. It is making your profile the clearest, most trustworthy answer for the services you actually want to book.

Why do some salons show up for "balayage near me" and others do not?

A general search like "hair salon near me" is mostly about your category and location. A service search like "balayage near me," "curly cut," "silk press" or "extensions" is about relevance to that specific service, and that is where many salons fall short. If nothing on your profile or website says you do balayage, Google has very little to match against.

Google lets eligible businesses list their services on the Business Profile, choosing from suggested services or adding custom ones, with descriptions and prices if you want. A salon whose profile lists color correction, balayage, lived-in blonde, keratin treatments and extensions, each with a short plain-language description, gives Google and guests far more to work with than one that just says "Hair Salon."

Your website matters here too. A single "Services" page with a price list is a start, but a real page for each service you want more of, with photos of your own work, who does it and what a first appointment looks like, backs up what your profile claims.

What does a strong salon Google Business Profile look like?

Think about it from the guest's side. They are comparing three or four salons on a small screen, often in under a minute. Here is what the profile should answer at a glance.

What the guest wants to knowWhat a strong profile shows
Do you do the service I want?The right primary category, plus a services list that names your key services in the words guests use
Is your work any good?Recent, real photos of finished color, cuts and styling, plus the space and the team
Do other guests like you?A steady stream of recent reviews with thoughtful replies from the owner or stylist
Can I get in soon?A booking link that opens straight to your online booking page, not your homepage
Where and when?Correct address, parking notes, accurate hours and holiday hours

On booking, Google lets you add booking links to your profile, and some salons can also connect a supported booking provider. Either way, the test is simple: tap it on your own phone and see whether a new guest can pick a service and a time without getting lost.

Do photos really matter on Google Maps?

For a salon, photos are the portfolio. A guest choosing a colorist for a big change wants to see work that looks like what they want. Google's photo tips for Business Profiles ask for photos that are in focus, well lit and free of heavy edits or excessive filters, so they show what a visit is really like. They also suggest adding work and team photos, not just the storefront.

What good looks like: fresh photos of real results in natural light, a few shots of the space and the stations, and the stylists themselves. Always ask your guest for permission before you post a photo of them or their hair, and keep a simple record that they said yes. Most guests are happy to be featured when you ask, and asking is part of treating them well.

How much do reviews matter for salon bookings?

Reviews do two jobs. Google counts them toward prominence, and guests read them to judge whether you are skilled, on time and kind. Google is not the only place guests read them. BrightLocal's 2026 Local Consumer Review Survey found that 71% of consumers used Google to read reviews, down from 83% the year before, so your reputation lives across several sites, with Google still a big one.

The reviews that help most mention the service and the stylist by name, because they show real people getting the result you want to be known for. Make asking for a review a normal part of checkout, never offer anything in exchange, and reply to every review in a warm, short, professional way. A calm reply to a tough review often reassures the next guest more than a perfect five stars.

Is Google Maps the only thing that matters now?

No. More guests now ask AI assistants for recommendations, and those tools often pull from the same public information: your Google profile, your website, your reviews and directory listings. Google says a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet to appear as a supporting link in its AI features, so ordinary search basics still apply. The salons that tend to come through clearly are the ones whose services, location and reviews say the same thing everywhere.

What should a salon check first?

  1. Search like a guest. On your phone, search "hair salon near me" and your top two services plus your neighborhood. Note who shows up and why.
  2. Check your categories and services. Make sure the services you most want to book are named clearly.
  3. Refresh your photos. Add recent, real, permission-cleared photos of your best work and your team.
  4. Test the booking path. Tap your booking link as if you were a new guest.
  5. Build a review habit. Ask every happy guest the same simple way, and reply to every review.

This is the kind of work we do with salons and independent stylists at The SocialDM, and you can see how it fits together on our hair salon marketing page.

Questions we hear

How does Google decide which salons show up for "hair salon near me"?

Google says local results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. A complete, accurate profile helps with relevance, and more reviews and positive ratings can help with prominence.

How can my salon show up for "balayage near me"?

Make it clear everywhere that you offer balayage: list it as a service on your Google Business Profile, give it its own page on your website with photos of your own work, and encourage guests to mention the service in reviews.

Can a salon pay Google to rank higher on Maps?

No. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Google Ads are a separate, paid product.

Should I add a booking link to my Google Business Profile?

Yes, if you take online bookings. Google lets you add booking links, and some businesses can connect a supported booking provider. Make sure the link opens your booking page, not your homepage.

Can I post photos of my guests' hair on Google and social media?

Only with their permission. Ask before you take or post the photo, and keep a simple record that they agreed.
